summary: The round-1 blocking fixes hold: code-build.md, fixer.md, review-judge.md and code-standards.md now carry stage wiring with ENG-n citations only, spec-builder.md restores the conventional-default runner clause, every pointer they name resolves in the shipped references, and all four dist harnesses are re-rendered and in sync — with one new low finding: the fix's own rewording in spec-builder.md left a three-item list ambiguous.

findings.summary: The SPEC-2 fix replaced a parenthetical with an unpaired em-dash, so the three-item plan-override list becomes ambiguous: the `Overridden:` clause can be read as continuing the test-runner appositive instead of the third list item.
findings.evidence: Line 31 now reads "`Test runner: <runner> - <why>` only when the repository has none — the language's conventional default, named with the reason so the user can object at the approver gate, and `Overridden: ENG-n - <repo rule that wins>` per override" — the em-dash appositive has no closing delimiter, so ", and `Overridden: ...`" parses either as the third item of the outer list or as part of the runner clause. tasks.md T006, the task this role text implements, words the same clause with parentheses — "(the language's conventional default, so the user can object at the approver gate)" — so the fix commit (7b0a931) drifted from its own spec's punctuation while fixing it. The constitution's Writing Standards (`.specify/memory/constitution.md`) require instructions to be "short, imperative and unambiguous"; a stateless spec-builder agent (constitution IV) re-reading this one long sentence on a fresh spawn can misattach the Overridden rule to the runner rule.
findings.fix: Restore a closed delimiter in core/roles/spec-builder.md line 31: "`Test runner: <runner> - <why>` only when the repository has none (the language's conventional default, named with the reason so the user can object at the approver gate), and `Overridden: ENG-n - <repo rule that wins>` per override or `Overridden: none`", then re-render all four harnesses and commit dist/ with the source (constitution III).
